pd_statement: As a Man Thinketh (1903) and Out from the Heart (1904) by James Allen (1864–1912) are in the public domain. This edition follows the early American printings; Allen’s wording and spelling are kept, the tables in Out from the Heart are set as lists, and obvious printing errors are corrected.

back.kicker: The classic of New Thought · Annotated Edition
headline: Mind is the master.
Thought builds character.
Change your thinking.
paras: “A man is literally what he thinks.” With these words James Allen, a self-taught English writer, gave the modern world one of its most quoted little books. Its sequel, Out from the Heart, turns the idea into daily discipline: how to watch the mind, form good habits and grow in character.

This beautifully designed annotated edition brings both classics together in one volume and adds what today’s reader needs: an introduction to Allen’s life and ideas, a plain-language note and a small practice after every chapter, and a guided 30-day practice.

parts.title: As a Man Thinketh
parts.label: Chapter
motto: Mind is the Master power that moulds and makes,
And Man is Mind, and evermore he takes
The tool of Thought, and, shaping what he wills,
Brings forth a thousand joys, a thousand ills:—
He thinks in secret, and it comes to pass:

parts.title: Out from the Heart
parts.label: Chapter
motto: Make pure thy heart, and thou wilt make thy life
Rich, sweet, and beautiful, unmarred by strife;
Guard well thy mind, and, noble, strong, and free,
Nothing shall harm, disturb, or conquer thee;
For all thy foes are in thy heart and mind.
There also thy salvation thou wilt find.
